account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary town business: my morning correspondence and market walk, reviewing town accounts, and afternoon tea with the neighbour on the east bank. The treasury contained 128 emeralds at 13:04, and I left it untouched. I have seen no bills or specific proposals. The secretary took the appointment book this morning to review the schedule and went to confirm the tea address, since the book only named a dockside cottage. We repeatedly missed each other's messages; I heard several indistinct calls. I eventually found the neighbour at the cottage at (16,105) and arrived late for tea. The neighbour said the secretary had kindly checked on it. That seems to explain the secretary's travel and calls, rather than indicating anything suspicious.

The only unusual information is the neighbour's vague, explicitly unconfirmed rumour about a bridge or port change. They had seen nothing urgent themselves and asked whether any changes had actually been proposed. I do not know of any proposal, who might be involved, or what such a change would be for. It is worth asking the secretary about, but not treating as established news. I returned to town hall for my 16:30 office time, reaching the office at 16:55. The appointments chest now contains a written book again, and the secretary is nearby. I have not yet read the returned book or heard her update.
